text: TEL MARIDUN, Aram Valley — Prof. Ansel Okafor led the excavation at Tel Maridun, according to people familiar with the matter, directing a three-season dig that uncovered a layered settlement sequence and a cache of inscribed clay tags. The team, operating under the Maridun Antiquities Survey, logged 412 catalogued objects between April and October, including storage jars, copper pins and a seal fragment bearing a river motif. Field notes reviewed by people familiar with the matter said Okafor coordinated trench planning, conservation and the final inventory submitted to the Dorn Institute last week. Associates said the excavation’s central square was opened on June 14 and produced the most significant finds, including a sealed ash pit and intact floor surfaces.
